But, here is a working example:

> raxml_file <- system.file("extdata/RAxML", "RAxML_bipartitionsBranchLabels.H3", package="ggtree")
> raxml <- read.raxml(raxml_file)
> p1<-ggtree(raxml) + geom_label(aes(label=bootstrap, fill=bootstrap)) + geom_tiplab() + geom_treescale()

#tree2
> nwk <- system.file("extdata", "sample.nwk", package="ggtree")
> p2 <- ggtree(read.tree(nwk)) %>% groupClade(node=21) + aes(color=group, linetype=group)  + geom_treescale()

Thank you

messages.subject: Re: Possible to sort branches so clades usually stay together?
messages.subject_clean: Possible to sort branches so clades usually stay together?
messages.body_plain:
This is not a comment on the code to rotate clades, but it looks like flipping your firmicutes clades to "keep them together" would be disingenuous. If the branch separating them is supported then the firmicutes are paraphyletic for whatever character(s)/sequence were used to build the tree. The long branch makes the placement possibly dubious, but the topology is the topology.

>
> As in the image above, there are often cases where sorting the leaves would allow clades to stay together. I am not sure if there is a standard way to do it. I know iTOL does it by sorting based on number of leaves in a branch (see Leaf sorting under Display modes here <http://itol.embl.de/help.cgi>).

>
